⁶ Then Naomi prepared to return from Moab with her daughters-in-law, because she had heard that the LORD had come to the aid of his people by providing food for them. ⁷ She set out from the place where she had been living, and her two daughters-in-law went with her along the road back to Judah. ⁸ Naomi said to them, "Go back, each of you, to your mother's home. Then she kissed them, and they all wept aloud. ¹⁰ They said to her, "We will go back with you to your people."

¹ Now Naomi had a relative on her husband's side, a prominent and wealthy man from Elimelech's family, whose name was Boaz. ² Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi, "Let me go to the fields and pick up the leftover grain behind anyone who will allow me to do so." As it turned out, she found herself working in the field belonging to Boaz, who was from the family of Elimelech. ⁴ Just then Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and greeted the harvesters, "The LORD be with you!" They answered, "The LORD bless you!" ⁵ Boaz asked the overseer of his harvesters, "Who does that young woman belong to?"

⁶ The overseer replied, "She is the Moabite woman who came back with Naomi from the country of Moab. ⁷ She asked, 'Please let me glean and gather among the sheaves behind the harvesters.' Don't go to glean in another field, and don't leave this one. Stay here close to my women workers. ⁹ Watch which fields they are harvesting and follow along after them. I have told the men not to lay a hand on you. And whenever you are thirsty, go drink from the water jars the men have filled." ¹⁰ At this, she bowed down with her face to the ground and asked him, "Why have I found such favor in your eyes that you notice me — a foreigner?"

And she lived with her mother-in-law.
